    AI Overview
    +9
    File a tax extension by submitting Form 4868 by April 15 to get an automatic six-month, interest-free (but not penalty-free) extension until October 15 to file. File electronically via IRS Free File or by paying your estimated tax debt using Direct Pay, selecting "Extension" as the reason. Note: This is an extension to file, not an extension to pay taxes due. 
    Methods to File an Extension (by April 15): 
    • IRS Free File: Use IRS Free File to electronically file Form 4868 for free, regardless of your income.
    • Pay Tax Due (Automatic Extension): Pay all or part of your estimated income tax due using Direct Pay, a debit/credit card, or the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS)
      . When you select "Extension" as the reason, the IRS automatically processes the extension, and you do not need to file Form 4868.
    • Tax Software: Most tax software providers (e.g., TurboTax, H&R Block) offer free federal extension filing.
    • Mail Paper Form 4868: Complete Form 4868 and mail it to the IRS, ensuring it is postmarked by April 15. 
    Key Considerations: 
    • Extension to File, Not Pay: You must estimate and pay any taxes owed by April 15 to avoid penalties.
    • Penalties: Late filing penalties can be up to 5% of the unpaid tax per month, while late payment penalties are generally 0.5% per month, with a maximum of 25%.
    • Disaster Relief: Victims of certain natural disasters may receive automatic extensions without filing Form 4868, as listed on the IRS disaster relief page.
    • State Extensions: A federal extension does not automatically extend your state tax deadline. Check your state's tax agency for specific requirements.

    What happens if I don't file a tax extension by April 15?
    The IRS has strict penalties for not hitting the April 15 deadline. Didn't file in time: You will be charged 5% of the unpaid tax every month or partial month the return is late, up to a maximum of 25%.     How to file for a tax extension

    While you will get more time to file your return, an extension does not grant you more time to pay your taxes. To avoid possible penalties, you should estimate and pay your federal taxes by the due date.

    Learn the ways to request an extension:
    • Online using IRS Free File
    • When you pay your estimated tax bill
    • Using IRS Form 4868
    How to pay taxes in installments

    If you feel that you may not be able to pay your tax bill in full by the due date, you may be eligible to pay in installments. Learn more about the IRS' payment plans and what additional costs and fees you may have to pay.
